cases.title: Profitable OEM instrument maker, temporary dip, leverage 2.1x, family stake 31%

It has not ruled out a sale, so the reject condition is not triggered. This is flagged for follow-up: a founder-held stake of this size is decisive for any take-private and needs early engagement. It is not a pass or a fail.
Regulatory: no matters reported, so there is no unresolved regulatory kill criterion.

Overall: no kill criterion is met and the thesis criteria are satisfied. This matches the thesis's own good-fit example (profitable OEM instrument maker, long supply contracts, sharp drop after a product transition, founding family with a large stake). Priority means we would buy at the right price. Actionable status depends on the code-computed takeout price against the target price, which is not assessed here.
Residual risks to verify in diligence: the platform ramp must deliver, and the family's willingness to sell is unknown. Neither is a thesis criterion that fails.

Management's comfort with the leverage and the lack of any planned disposal do not change the outcome. That is a management opinion, not a data point, and the kill criterion is quantitative. The leverage also followed an acquisition, so it is unlikely to fall quickly without EBITDA recovery, which is itself exposed to the destocking cycle.

Otherwise the company fits the strategy well: in-vitro diagnostics (clinical chemistry analyzers with captive reagents), recurring revenue at 68% of sales (above the 50% threshold), EBITDA margin of 18%, and a market cap of EUR 540m, which is mid-sized.

Only the leverage kill criterion is met, so the verdict is Reject rather than Radar. If leverage drops below 4x on a later data refresh, for example through EBITDA recovery or debt paydown, the company would be a strong Priority candidate and should be re-screened. Rejecting now should not mean forgetting it.

cases.title: Fits everything except the recurring-revenue rule (20% recurring)
reasons: Segment: Lab automation systems is an in-vitro diagnostics segment we like, so there is no segment downgrade.

Kill criteria: none met. Net debt/EBITDA is 1.5x (data figure), well below the 4x limit. No holder is above 25% (largest is management and founders at 15%), so there is no controlling shareholder and no stated refusal to sell. No regulatory issue is reported.

Price drop: this looks temporary. The 30% 12-month fall followed two large hospital-network orders slipping from 2025 to 2026, and both have since been confirmed. That is timing, not a structural loss of market. The 3-month change of -4% shows no further deterioration. This supports the thesis.

Business model: service is only 20% of sales, against the thesis benchmark of at least 50% recurring revenue. The rule is a warning only and never a reject, but it matters. The company sells capital equipment, so revenue is lumpy and depends on order timing. This is the same mechanism that caused the drop. The thesis wants recurring revenue (consumables, service, supply contracts), and this company does not have that profile.
Profitability: the 14% LTM EBITDA margin is positive but modest. There is no evidence of the long supply contracts that characterise a good fit.

cases.title: Real data: Stratec (SBS.DE), facts limited to the dataset
reasons: Segment fit: Stratec is an OEM analyzer and lab automation maker for IVD, squarely in the segments we like. This is not a reason to downgrade.

Kill criterion, leverage: net debt/EBITDA is 3.41x, taken from the data. That is below the 4x threshold, so it is not triggered, but the headroom is thin (EBITDA of 28m against debt of 116m). Leverage would matter for an LBO.

Kill criterion, controlling shareholder: insiders hold 61.1%, which is far above the 25% flag threshold. The dataset names no holder and gives no stake or statement on a sale. Yahoo lists at most the top 5 institutions, and family or strategic holders may be missing. We do not know who controls the stake or whether they have ruled out a sale, and an unknown is never a pass. With a 61% insider block, a sale is impossible without their consent, so this is the key open fact. Flag: holder unknown, stake about 61% (insiders), no public statement on selling in the data.

Why the price is low: the dataset does not say why the price moved. Financials show pressure: revenue fell from 270m (2023) to 258m (2024) to 251m (2025), and EBITDA fell from 47m (2024) to 34m (2025). The LTM EBITDA margin is 11.6%. This is consistent with either a temporary product transition and destocking, or a structural share loss. Headlines mention a 'Strong Q2 Recovery' and a +23% 3-month price move, which hints at temporary weakness, but that is not proof. The 12-month change is -15%. The thesis requires the drop to be temporary, and that is unverified.
Business model: the share of recurring revenue (consumables, service) is not in the data. This is a warning only and never a reject, but it is unconfirmed.
Profitability: the company is profitable, with EBITDA of about 28m on 244.8m revenue, but margins are compressed.

Conclusion: it fits the strategy (OEM IVD analyzers, profitable, German, mid-sized, large insider stake), and no kill criterion is demonstrably met. Two key facts are unknown: whether the controlling holder would sell, and whether the price drop is temporary. So it cannot be Priority. It is not a Reject either, because there is no evidence of a ruled-out sale or an unresolved regulatory issue. Radar. Next steps: identify the controlling holder, find any public statement on a sale, and check the H1-2026 release and call for the cause of the weakness and the recurring revenue share.

cases.title: Real data: QuidelOrtho (QDEL), net debt 6.1x EBITDA
reasons: Kill criterion met: net debt/EBITDA is 6.09x (code-computed: debt 3,076m, cash 123m, EBITDA 485m), well above the 4x limit. The figure comes from the data, not from the judge. Under the thesis, any kill criterion means Reject.
Segment fit is fine: immunoassay and point-of-care is in-vitro diagnostics (instruments and assays). That does not offset the leverage kill.

Profitability is doubtful. LTM EBITDA margin is 18.1%, but FY2024 EBITDA was -1,490m and FY2025 was -483m. These look like large one-off charges such as impairments, but the dataset doesn't say so. The thesis wants profitable companies.

Why the price is low is unknown. The shares are down 54% over 12 months and 22% over 3 months. The dataset gives no cause, and none of the headlines explain it. We cannot confirm the drop is temporary, so on its own this would be Radar.
Recurring revenue share is not in the data. It is a warning only under the thesis.

Ownership: no holder is above 25%. The largest are BlackRock 16.3%, FMR 10.7% and Newtyn 9.7%. Insiders hold 0.9%. There is no controlling shareholder and no public statement on a sale. No ownership flag applies.
Regulatory issues are not in the dataset, so they remain unknown and are not treated as a pass.

Leverage is also a practical problem for a take-private. With market cap at EUR 790m against EV of EUR 3,425m, existing debt is already about 4x equity value. Adding LBO financing would be hard, and it could still be a fit if the company deleveraged. Re-screen if net debt/EBITDA falls below 4x.
